concerns: This submission intentionally keeps operational decision data inside observations[] because unsupported top-level keys are dropped by runtime normalization.

findings.claim: The CLI currently has no example command dispatch or help surface, so implementation must add a new command family rather than wiring into existing lifecycle aliases.
Stable example-specific failures require public error-code work because existing error normalization turns unknown contract codes into internal_error.
The npm payload currently cannot satisfy gallery publication acceptance because examples/sample-projects is not in the package allowlist and package:check is only npm pack --dry-run.

observations.detail: Own gallery behavior in new focused modules: src/examples/catalog.js validates the single catalog and source roots; src/examples/list.js maps catalog entries to human and JSON payloads; src/examples/copy.js owns destination preflight, staging, cleanup, and receipt data; src/examples/index.js exposes listExamples and copyExample for CLI use. Keep src/cli.js as command router and output caller only, matching current central dispatch and catch envelope authority. Add packaged data under examples/sample-projects with the exact ten confirmed IDs from spec.md Confirmed Scope; package.json must include that gallery because current npm allowlist omits examples.
observations.title: Module ownership

observations.detail: Consumer inputs: launchdeck example list plus existing --json, --compact, --no-color flags from parseArgs; catalog loader; terminal columns/noColor from io/runtime. Producer outputs: human scan list of exactly ten entries, or one schemaVersion 1 success envelope command=example list with entries derived exactly from catalog fields id,title,stack,theme,requirements,ports,sourcePath. No prompts, no filesystem mutation, no Launchdeck config lookup. Compact must go through output.js compact handling rather than a separate schema authority.
observations.title: List interface map

observations.detail: Consumer inputs: launchdeck example copy [id] [destination], catalog lookup, optional TTY searchable selector only when id is omitted and json is false and terminal is TTY, and destination default path.resolve(cwd,id). Producer outputs: success receipt only after rename publishes the copied tree, or stable typed outcomes for unknown ID, missing ID without TTY, no-match, cancel, destination conflict, catalog/source invalid, copy failure, and rename failure. The command must not install dependencies, run projects, initialize Git, write .launchdeck.yml, access network, or touch Launchdeck runtime state.
observations.title: Copy interface map

observations.detail: Algorithm: load catalog and validate exact ten unique IDs; resolve source path below examples/sample-projects using path.resolve plus inside-root check; lstat source tree and reject symlinks, .launchdeck.yml, Launchdeck artifacts, and missing dirs; resolve destination and parent; reject existing destination of any type with lstat before staging; create a unique staging directory in the same destination parent using fs.mkdtemp with a hidden basename prefix; copy recursively into staging; recheck destination absence immediately before publish; fs.rename staging to destination; on any pre-rename or copy failure rm staging recursively and leave destination absent; on rename failure attempt rm staging and any owned unpublished destination only if safe, then return typed failure. Same-parent staging is required for same-filesystem rename; use a target-specific lock directory or lock file to reduce Launchdeck concurrent copies.
observations.title: Atomic destination algorithm

observations.detail: Do not couple sample sources to Launchdeck. Compatibility proof should be an external fixture that copies each sample to a temp dir, creates a reviewable candidate .launchdeck.yml outside the sample source, runs doctor and applicable setup/build/test/start/HTTP-or-API-health/stop, then cleans in finally. Gallery copy must not register projects or mutate .launchdeck runtime state as a side effect.
observations.title: Lifecycle compatibility architecture

observations.detail: Expand package files and repository contract tests so the actual npm tarball contains exactly the gallery plus existing package surfaces, with packed <=5 MiB and unpacked <=20 MiB. Current package scripts only run build-agent-plugins prepack and npm pack --dry-run; current CI package job only runs npm audit and npm run package:check on ubuntu. Add a package inventory gate that snapshots ten catalog sources and forbidden files, and add Windows/Linux native matrix checks for sample install/test/start/health/stop without making sample dependencies part of root npm ci.
observations.title: Packaging and CI gates

observations.detail: The implementation inventory is exactly vite-react-habit-tracker, nextjs-blog-manager, nestjs-url-shortener, fastapi-inventory, django-events, go-webhook-inbox, spring-boot-orders, aspnet-library-catalog, docker-compose-helpdesk, and node-python-issue-tracker under examples/sample-projects. This is not an extensibility promise; additions, replacement, merge, or reduction require reopening scope.
observations.title: Confirmed ten-project inventory

observations.detail: CA-001 protects npm size without reducing sample scope; CA-002 requires repairing failed sample/OS cells rather than skipping; CA-003 requires no published or staging residue after cancel/filesystem failure; CA-004 blocks release on repository/catalog/copied/tarball mismatch. The OCD observations carry these refs outcome-by-outcome in runtime-preserved observation entries.
observations.title: Consequence analysis mapping

decision.cancel_behavior: Not applicable; list has no interactive cancel state.
decision.consumer_owner: human TTY, human non-TTY, JSON automation
decision.interaction_policy: No prompt; render human scan list or one schemaVersion 1 JSON/compact object from catalog only.
decision.recovery_cleanup: If catalog read fails, do not emit partial entries; route to OUT-EX-CATALOG-INVALID.
decision.retry_identity: Same invocation is safe and idempotent because no filesystem mutation occurs.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if list output is not derived from the single catalog, omits any of the ten confirmed IDs, emits more than one JSON object, or relies on color for meaning.

decision.cancel_behavior: No cancel after mutation boundary; before staging, cancel routes to OUT-EX-CANCEL.
decision.consumer_owner: CLI caller and destination parent filesystem
decision.interaction_policy: Explicit ID is deterministic; omitted ID may use TTY selector before mutation; receipt is emitted only after rename succeeds.
decision.recovery_cleanup: No cleanup after successful publish except fixture teardown in tests; published destination is user-owned result.
decision.request_retention: Receipt retains selected ID, source catalog entry, and resolved destination.
decision.retry_identity: Same command after success is a new invocation that must fail as destination conflict, not overwrite.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if success can be reported before atomic rename, if retry overwrites, or if copied tree includes Launchdeck artifacts.

decision.cancel_behavior: No mutation and no cancel state.
decision.interaction_policy: Return command_usage_error with valid example syntax; do not load catalog, prompt, stage, or mutate filesystem.
decision.recovery_cleanup: No cleanup needed because operation is refused before dispatch.
decision.request_retention: Caller keeps original args externally; response gives corrected command shape.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if invalid syntax reaches catalog/copy execution or emits unstable/internal error codes.

decision.interaction_policy: Typed package-integrity failure; no partial list, no selector options, and no copy attempt.
decision.recovery_cleanup: No destination staging may exist; failure happens before copy preflight.
decision.request_retention: None; package/source must be repaired before retry.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if catalog accepts duplicate IDs, missing IDs, escaped paths, extra fields, or mismatched source roots.

decision.cancel_behavior: Omit retry or cancel by ending command; no mutation occurred.
decision.interaction_policy: Recoverable user input; explicit retry only with a valid catalog ID or use example list.
decision.recovery_cleanup: No staging created; destination remains absent.
decision.request_retention: Retain destination and flags; replace ID.
decision.security_constraints: Resolve IDs only by exact catalog key before any path resolution; never interpolate raw ID into filesystem paths; expose only catalog IDs as safe alternatives.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if unknown ID is treated as path input, creates a destination, or hides valid recovery action.

decision.cancel_behavior: Do not retry automatically; no prompt cancellation exists.
decision.interaction_policy: Recoverable user input; never prompt in non-TTY, --json, or --compact modes; require explicit ID.
decision.recovery_cleanup: No staging created; no terminal decoration in JSON.
decision.request_retention: Retain destination and flags; add explicit ID.
decision.security_constraints: No TTY UI or terminal prose in machine mode; do not infer sample ID from cwd, destination, environment, or partial user text.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if JSON/non-TTY emits prompt text, blocks waiting for input, or mutates filesystem before ID.

decision.cancel_behavior: Typed cancellation leaves no target or staging path.
decision.interaction_policy: Recoverable user input inside omitted-ID TTY flow; retain query, show explicit no-match state, allow edit or cancellation before mutation.
decision.recovery_cleanup: No filesystem action before a valid catalog selection.
decision.request_retention: Retain in-session query and destination preview only until selection/cancel.
decision.retry_identity: Same prompt session until selection, edited query, or cancel.
decision.security_constraints: Search filters catalog records only; query must not probe arbitrary filesystem paths, shell commands, network, or package metadata beyond the catalog.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if no-match exits as unknown ID without edit path, creates staging, or offers non-catalog choices.

decision.cancel_behavior: Return cancelled outcome/effect none; no destination and no staging residue.
decision.interaction_policy: Cancellation is a typed no-effect outcome before copy preflight; do not convert to success copy or filesystem failure.
decision.recovery_cleanup: No staging should exist; if a selector implementation allocates preview state, discard it in memory.
decision.request_retention: None; user starts a new command if desired.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if cancel exits with success receipt, leaves staging/target, or loses typed cancelled behavior.

decision.cancel_behavior: No staging created; no cleanup beyond releasing any in-memory lock.
decision.consumer_owner: CLI caller and destination parent filesystem
decision.interaction_policy: Reject any existing destination path of any type before staging; no overwrite, merge, or prompt-to-overwrite mode.
decision.recovery_cleanup: Destination remains untouched; staging path must not exist.
decision.request_retention: Retain selected ID; caller chooses absent destination.
decision.retry_identity: New invocation with a non-existing destination.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if existing empty directories are allowed, if --force/overwrite appears, or if conflict is detected after partial copy.

decision.interaction_policy: Typed package/source integrity failure when catalog source is missing, escaped, impure, or mismatched with tarball/source snapshot; no copy attempt.
decision.recovery_cleanup: Destination must remain absent; no staging created.
decision.request_retention: None; package/source inventory must be repaired.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if source drift is tolerated, release continues, or copy fabricates sample content.

decision.cancel_behavior: No interactive cancel during copy; interruption/failure must cleanup staging before returning.
decision.consumer_owner: CLI caller and destination parent filesystem
decision.interaction_policy: Terminal filesystem failure after automatic cleanup; user explicitly retries after fixing permissions/disk/source.
decision.recovery_cleanup: Remove staging recursively; destination remains absent; release blocks on any residue.
decision.request_retention: Error retains ID, destination, and staging failure details sufficient for explicit retry.
decision.retry_identity: New invocation with new staging identity.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if staging remains, destination partially appears, failure is reported as success, or retry reuses stale staging.

decision.cancel_behavior: No cancel during rename; cleanup owned staging and any owned unpublished destination if safe.
decision.consumer_owner: CLI caller and destination parent filesystem
decision.interaction_policy: Terminal filesystem failure; never fall back to merge/copy-over publish; explicit user retry after cleanup/inspection.
decision.recovery_cleanup: Remove staging; remove only owned unpublished destination artifact if created by failed rename; otherwise report indeterminate cleanup and block release.
decision.request_retention: Error retains ID, destination, and publish failure details.
decision.retry_identity: New invocation after inspecting parent/destination; new staging identity.
decision.stop_reopen_condition: Reopen if implementation falls back to non-atomic copy, leaves staging, overwrites existing target, or cannot prove no residue after rename failure.
